question.text: Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>10</mn><mi>cos</mi><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mi>cm</mi></math>. The amplitude of the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position, for that

sin2πtT=1

Therefore, A=10cos43π=10×12= 5 cm
